title: Median of two sorted arrays
statement: Return the median of the union of two sorted arrays (not both empty) in O(log(min(m, n))).
hints: The median splits the union into two equal halves. Choose how many elements the left half takes from the shorter array: i; then j = half − i from the other.
The split is right when a[i−1] ≤ b[j] and b[j−1] ≤ a[i]; binary-search i.

solution.explanation: Binary-search the number i of elements the left half takes from the shorter array (j = half − i from the other). The partition is valid when the left maxima don't exceed the right minima on the opposite side; if a[i−1] > b[j], i is too big, else too small. Sentinels ±∞ handle the edges. It's binary search on a partition, the hardest classic of the family.
